Meanwhile, the weekly pricing power indicator rose to seventy-three, reflecting ongoing momentum in transportation markets and shifting dynamics across domestic logistics networks.

headline: Refrigerated truckload tender rejections double year-over-year
summary: Refrigerated truckload tender rejections have surged to 23 percent during Thanksgiving week, doubling the rates seen during the same period last year. This sharp increase indicates a severe supply-driven capacity crunch rather than a shift in consumer demand. The tightening capacity is expected to place upward pressure on spot rates and disrupt contract tenders across the freight market as the holiday season progresses.

headline: Bulker Refloated off French Coast After Four Days
summary: Salvage teams successfully pulled the grounded bulk carrier Miro G free from the shoreline along France's Atlantic coast. The Malta-flagged vessel had been stranded near Lit-et-Mixe for four days after being driven onto the beach. An emergency response tug operated by Les Abeilles International executed the refloating operation on Tuesday afternoon, mitigating potential disruptions to regional maritime logistics and shipping lanes.

headline: Danaos secures $611m in new containership charters
summary: Greek containership owner Danaos has added $611 million in contracted revenue through recent fixture agreements and charter extensions, boosting its total forward revenue backlog to $5 billion. The transactions involve fresh contracts for six newly built containerships, according to the company's latest quarterly financial update. This commercial activity extends the operational employment schedule for a significant portion of its fleet, providing long-term revenue visibility amid ongoing market fluctuations.

headline: EnEarth Acquires Stake in Scottish Carbon Storage Project
summary: Carbon storage developer EnEarth has agreed to purchase Storegga's thirty percent stake in the Acorn carbon capture and storage initiative located in northeast Scotland. With this transaction, EnEarth assumes the role of lead developer for the North Sea scheme. The agreement involves transferring all project interests, ongoing development duties, and the existing management team and personnel from Storegga to EnEarth, shifting the operational leadership of the regional carbon reduction infrastructure undertaking.

headline: Torvald Klaveness estimates $7B in dry bulk and tanker inefficiencies
summary: A recent study by Norwegian shipping group Torvald Klaveness highlights roughly $7 billion in potential yearly savings within the dry bulk and product tanker sectors. The research evaluates total annual freight expenditures and points to excessive transaction costs, suboptimal vessel utilization, and inadequate port coordination as primary drivers of operational waste. Addressing these structural shortcomings could significantly optimize maritime logistics and reduce overall transportation expenses.

headline: New Hamburg Shipmanagement Firm Targets Complex Vessel Niche
summary: Two industry professionals have launched a specialized shipmanagement company in Hamburg to serve vessels involved in unconventional operations. The new venture combines extensive commercial shipping experience with legal expertise in the maritime sector, aiming to address specialized demands within the global fleet market.

headline: COSCO starts direct China-to-Greece Ro-Ro vehicle shipping lane
summary: COSCO SHIPPING Specialized Carriers has inaugurated a direct roll-on/roll-off maritime route linking Shenzhen's Xiaomo Port with Astakos Port in Greece. The inaugural voyage commenced with the departure of the vessel Yuan He Kou, which transported 4,898 Chinese-manufactured new energy vehicles. This new logistics connection aims to streamline vehicle export distribution from manufacturing hubs in Asia directly into the European market, enhancing maritime freight options for the growing electric vehicle sector.

headline: Maersk Cuts Intermodal Fuel Fees in Australia and New Zealand
summary: Ocean carrier Maersk is lowering its landside intermodal fuel fees across Australia and New Zealand starting December 1, 2026. In five Australian states, the surcharge will drop from 25 percent to 22 percent. Meanwhile, the fee in New Zealand will see a steeper reduction, falling from 27 percent to 23 percent. These adjusted rates will remain in effect through January 31, 2027, reflecting adjustments in regional landside transportation and fuel cost dynamics.

headline: Colombo Port Reports 10% Rise in Transshipment Volumes
summary: The Port of Colombo experienced a significant increase in cargo activity, processing over six million TEUs of transshipment containers between January and October. This performance reflects a ten percent growth compared to the corresponding timeframe in the previous year. Momentum persisted through October, which saw a nearly ten percent year-on-year rise in monthly volume handled, highlighting the facility's expanding role as a regional maritime hub.

headline: Maersk sets North American document amendment fee
summary: Container shipping line Maersk has announced a new Transport Document Amendment Fee applicable to specific shipments originating from United States and Canadian ports. Scheduled to take effect in January 2027, the policy imposes a seventy-five dollar charge on qualifying modification requests made three or more calendar days following the loading of containers onto the vessel.

headline: Seatrium reduces Singapore workforce in shipyard consolidation
summary: Singapore-based marine engineering provider Seatrium is cutting roughly two percent of its local workforce as part of a broader corporate restructuring initiative. The strategic move is designed to streamline operations, consolidate shipyard facilities, and better align company resources with upcoming project demands. This reduction represents the organization's initial workforce reorganization following its merger in 2023, reflecting ongoing efforts to enhance overall manufacturing and operational efficiency within its maritime supply chain infrastructure.

headline: Port of Gothenburg Upgrades Rail Infrastructure for Electrification
summary: The Port of Gothenburg is enhancing its container terminal handling tracks with overhead line infrastructure to support direct electric locomotive operations. This initiative eliminates reliance on diesel engines and bypass routes through the departure yard. The upgrade aims to boost throughput capacity, lower emissions, and streamline rail logistics for greater efficiency.

headline: Nord Gas Solutions wins HD Hyundai contract for two VLGCs
summary: Nord Gas Solutions has been awarded a contract by HD Hyundai to provide cargo handling and liquefied petroleum gas fuel supply systems for two Very Large Gas Carriers. The 90,000 cubic meter vessels are being constructed for Transpetrol at the HD Hyundai Samho Heavy Industries shipyard located in South Korea. These specialized carriers are designed to transport liquefied petroleum gas, supporting the maritime sector's ongoing infrastructure and vessel outfitting requirements for cleaner fuel technologies.

headline: cargo-partner and Nippon Express restructure European logistics
summary: cargo-partner is reorganizing its European operations to integrate more deeply with Nippon Express Holdings, targeting strategic growth through 2027. The restructuring emphasizes Central and Eastern European markets, allowing cargo-partner to maintain its distinct operational identity while leveraging the parent company's network. This organizational adjustment aims to optimize regional infrastructure and strengthen market positioning across key European supply chain corridors.

headline: EU Proposes Ban on Russian-Insured Tankers and Energy Services
summary: The European Union has introduced a new sanctions package targeting Russian energy trade. The measures include a ban on tankers carrying Russian insurance coverage and a prohibition on European firms providing construction, operational, or repair services for Russian energy infrastructure, specifically refineries. These restrictions are expected to cause further disruptions to global crude and refined product trade flows as the bloc continues to tighten economic pressure.

headline: Strait of Hormuz Crude Freight Rates Outperform Wider Market
summary: Crude oil tanker earnings demonstrated a distinct divergence between routes operating inside and outside the Strait of Hormuz. While freight rates outside the strategic waterway surrendered the majority of their recent gains, transit costs within the Strait maintained their elevated premiums. This sustained strength was driven by steady regional crude transfer networks meeting replenishment demand from Asian markets, supporting continued maritime tonnage movement along the eastern routes despite broader market softening.

headline: China Resumes US Soybean Purchases
summary: Chinese imports of US soybeans rebounded during September and October, reaching approximately 4.3 million metric tons compared to minimal volumes during the previous trade dispute period. Projections indicate that overall US soybean shipments to China could increase by roughly 15 percent over the upcoming multi-year agricultural seasons, reflecting a shift toward heavier purchasing activity directly during the harvest period. Concurrently, US wheat exports experienced a significant decline, dropping by approximately one-third.

headline: Evaluating 200,000m³ LNG Carriers for Fleet Renewal
summary: A recent technical and commercial assessment explores the viability of 200,000m³ liquefied natural gas carriers for future fleet updates. The study weighs the efficiency benefits of larger cargo capacities against potential limitations imposed by existing port and terminal infrastructure constraints. Ship operators and industry stakeholders are analyzing whether these ultra-large vessels can balance transport economics with global supply chain compatibility, or if their increased scale will restrict them from accessing key trade routes and facilities.

headline: Tresco Group expands into maritime shipping with Green Maritime buyout
summary: Antwerp-based inland navigation software provider Tresco Group has acquired Dutch operational data specialist Green Maritime. The transaction enables Tresco to extend its technological reach from inland waterways into the broader seagoing shipping sector. Green Maritime currently provides onboard data solutions for over two hundred vessels, predominantly within short sea shipping operations, positioning the combined entity to address evolving maritime regulatory and environmental demands.

headline: Tight Bunker Fuel Supplies Persist in Singapore and Malaysia
summary: Bunker fuel availability remains constrained across Singapore and Malaysia, with terminal loading slots and barge capacity heavily booked through November, and early December bookings already underway. Meanwhile, very low sulfur fuel oil lead times have experienced a slight reduction, dropping to twelve to fourteen days, while high sulfur fuel oil lead times hover near previous levels. These ongoing capacity constraints highlight continued pressure on regional maritime logistics and bunkering operations.

headline: Shippers Urged to Prioritize Supply Chain Flexibility Over Cost
summary: Supply chain experts warn that shippers compromise their resilience when transport contracts are awarded solely based on lowest price. Analysts note that logistics providers offer minimal protection during capacity crunches or rising costs when operating on unsustainably low margins. While diversifying transport networks is a common strategy to mitigate disruption, experts caution that relying on financially strained providers creates a false sense of security. True commercial value in modern logistics stems from operational flexibility rather than purely cost-driven procurement strategies.

headline: Maersk and ONE Reportedly Planning Global North-South Alliance
summary: Container shipping giants Maersk and Ocean Network Express are reportedly developing a vessel-sharing agreement to establish the first global liner alliance covering north-south trade routes. Historically, ocean carriers have managed north-south trades through separate, route-specific partnerships depending on the individual market dynamics. Industry sources indicate that the two companies are now working toward a comprehensive global arrangement, marking a potential shift in how international maritime networks and capacity are organized across these corridors.

headline: Artificial Intelligence disrupts logistics capital and freight valuations
summary: Artificial intelligence investments have significantly impacted the logistics sector by competing for financial capital, disrupting traditional freight broker valuations, and driving selective market rotation. While massive venture capital and corporate debt flows heavily favored technology assets, the broader logistics landscape experienced distinct market pressures as investors reassessed the integration and valuation of technology within supply chain operations.

headline: Gulftainer and CULines Partner to Boost China-Gulf Capacity
summary: A strategic partnership between port operator Gulftainer and carrier CULines will secure priority operating rights at the United Arab Emirates' Khor Fakkan Port. This collaboration is set to drive a significant expansion of container capacity along the China-Persian Gulf trade corridor. As carriers navigate an increasingly volatile global trade environment, the move aims to capture sustained growth opportunities in the region by enhancing port access and operational efficiency across key Middle Eastern maritime hubs.

headline: Simple Cargo increases volume via cargo management automation
summary: Air cargo broker Simple Cargo handles approximately 30 percent more shipments without increasing headcount, following the implementation of an integrated cargo management system. Operating across the Netherlands and Belgium, the company utilized software that consolidates sales, bookings, and invoicing. This digital transformation significantly reduced daily administrative workloads, cutting the time spent on booking tasks from a full working day for a single employee down to a fraction, thereby boosting operational efficiency and enabling business growth without expanding staff.

headline: Mexico Approves Expansion Plan for Port of Manzanillo
summary: Mexico's environmental agency has granted conditional approval for the initial phase of the multi-billion dollar Puerto Nuevo Manzanillo project. The massive infrastructure initiative aims to significantly expand the Pacific port's operating footprint and eventually triple its container throughput capacity to accommodate rising cargo volumes. Asipona Manzanillo, the port administration, advanced the revised proposal following sustained growth in container traffic at the country's primary Pacific gateway.

headline: Procter & Gamble plans workforce cuts amid supply chain automation
summary: Consumer packaged goods leader Procter & Gamble intends to reduce its product-supply workforce by up to 30 percent by the year 2030. The planned reductions are driven by an ongoing expansion of automation within the company's supply chain operations. This strategic shift reflects a broader industry trend toward technology-driven efficiencies in manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution networks as companies seek to streamline operations and lower long-term labor costs while maintaining high-volume output across their global distribution footprints.

headline: Under Armour plans deeper SKU cuts to streamline supply chain
summary: Athletic apparel brand Under Armour is expanding its portfolio rationalization strategy by targeting a fifty percent reduction in its product assortment. Having already achieved a twenty-five percent cut earlier in the year, the company aims to simplify operational decision-making and concentrate resources on its core, high-performing merchandise. This ongoing inventory optimization effort is designed to shorten lead times and improve overall efficiency across the supply chain.

headline: Diesel Prices Experience Record Weekly Drop
summary: Retail diesel prices saw their largest one-week decline in recent history, dropping significantly to $5.695 per gallon according to the Energy Information Administration. This sharp reduction reflects a broader reset in global oil markets that is quickly passing through to fuel surcharges paid by shippers and logistics operators. The falling costs provide near-term financial relief for freight carriers and supply chain networks heavily reliant on diesel fuel for over-the-road transportation and distribution operations.

headline: J.B. Hunt Opposes Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Merger
summary: J.B. Hunt has formally filed with the Surface Transportation Board, urging regulators to deny the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The trucking company challenged the rail carriers' projected truck-to-rail freight conversions and requested that regulators establish enforceable protective measures should the consolidation move forward. This regulatory challenge highlights ongoing industry concerns regarding rail market competition and the broader impacts on intermodal logistics networks and freight capacity.

headline: Very Large Gas Carrier freight rates hit historic highs
summary: The very large gas carrier sector is experiencing an unprecedented bull market, with daily earnings approaching record levels of $250,000. These extraordinary freight rates on benchmark routes are proving lucrative enough to incentivize ethane carriers to shift operations into liquefied petroleum gas trades, shifting capacity dynamics within the maritime logistics market.

headline: Starlink launches high-speed maritime internet for merchant ships
summary: Elon Musk's satellite operator has introduced a premium maritime internet package designed to deliver gigabit speeds to merchant vessels. Priced significantly higher than standard offerings, this high-bandwidth connectivity solution aims to transform vessel operations, routine maintenance, and crew communications at sea. By bridging the digital divide for commercial fleets, the technology enhances real-time data exchange between ship and shore, potentially streamlining logistics management, remote vessel monitoring, and overall supply chain visibility across global maritime routes.

headline: Black Sea Shipping Crisis Prompts New Sanctions and Grain Talks
summary: The European Commission is advancing a new sanctions package aimed at banning Russian-insured tankers as the maritime impacts of the Ukraine conflict expand. Simultaneously, the United Nations is advocating for a renewed humanitarian shipping framework to facilitate grain exports through the Black Sea. These diplomatic and regulatory measures highlight ongoing efforts to secure maritime trade routes and mitigate supply chain disruptions affecting regional food and energy distribution networks.

headline: Thenamaris orders two VLCCs at Chinese shipyard
summary: Greek shipowner Thenamaris has expanded its maritime construction portfolio by contracting two 303,000 dwt crude carriers with China's New Times Shipbuilding. The scrubber-fitted vessels have been officially added to the company's updated registry, with both newbuilds scheduled for delivery in the year 2030. Financial terms regarding the transaction were not disclosed in the announcement, marking the firm's re-entry into the very large crude carrier ordering sector.

headline: K Line Orders Two LPG Carriers from HD Hyundai Samho
summary: Japanese shipping company Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha has contracted HD Hyundai Samho in South Korea to build two LPG dual-fuel very large gas carriers. The 90,000 cubic meter vessels, designed to support the expansion of United States liquefied petroleum gas trade, are slated for delivery in the year 2030. This initiative expands the firm's existing maritime asset portfolio within the global energy shipping sector, reflecting ongoing fleet modernization efforts to accommodate shifting energy trade routes.

headline: Inui Global Logistics Expands Bulk Fleet to 40 Ships by 2030
summary: Japanese maritime operator Inui Global Logistics plans to grow its handysize bulk carrier fleet significantly by the end of the decade. The Tokyo-listed company aims to reach a total of forty ships by March 2030, which includes more than doubling its long-term chartered tonnage. This strategic fleet expansion is driven by expectations of a tightening dry bulk shipping market and increasing demand for maritime freight capacity over the coming years.

headline: Arcadia Shipmanagement expands Suezmax tanker order in South Korea
summary: Greek shipowner Arcadia Shipmanagement has significantly expanded its vessel newbuilding programme by exercising options for two additional Suezmax crude oil carriers at South Korea’s HD Hyundai. The deal, valued at approximately $196 million, covers 157,000 deadweight tonnage vessels priced at around $98 million each. These new ships are scheduled for delivery to the company's expanding fleet over the coming period, boosting its capacity for maritime crude oil logistics and freight operations.

headline: Maritime Charterparty Rules on Accepting Part Cargoes
summary: Shipowners considering an additional part cargo for an already fixed voyage must first review their existing charterparty agreement. Industry experts note that charterers frequently prohibit the carriage of extra freight. If restrictions are present in the contract, owners are required to secure explicit permission from the primary charterer before proceeding, highlighting the importance of careful contract navigation in maritime logistics and shipping operations.

headline: Maersk Cuts Canadian Container Drayage Fuel Surcharge
summary: Ocean carrier Maersk has announced a reduction in its Export and Import Fuel Surcharges for Canadian container drayage. The surcharge applied to inland haulage between marine terminals and initial inland nodes will drop from 24% to 20%. The adjustment is scheduled to take effect on December 1, 2026, and will be subject to ongoing monthly reviews by the carrier to reflect fluctuating transportation energy costs.

headline: Circle Group Releases MasterSPED 10.4 Freight Platform
summary: Circle Group has introduced MasterSPED 10.4, an upgraded software solution developed by NEXT Freight to integrate freight forwarding, customs procedures, and financial administration into one workflow. The updated version incorporates enhanced automation capabilities for managing shipments, handling customs paperwork, and overseeing financial tasks across sea, road, and air transport modes via a centralized dashboard.

headline: OOCL Adds Third Methanol Dual-Fuel Containership
summary: Orient Overseas Container Line recently celebrated the naming ceremony for the OOCL Faith, marking the addition of its third 24,000 TEU methanol dual-fuel containership to its fleet. The vessel was christened during an event held at the Nantong COSCO KHI Ship Engineering shipyard in China. This latest delivery highlights ongoing efforts by ocean carriers to incorporate alternative-fuel vessels into their global networks as part of broader fleet modernization and decarbonization initiatives within the maritime logistics sector.

headline: Container freight rates drop amid Transpacific market weakness
summary: Global container shipping costs continued to decline as demand weakened across major trade lanes. Drewry's World Container Index dropped three percent to four thousand one hundred seventy-six dollars per forty-foot box, marking four straight weeks of decreases. Simultaneously, the NYSHEX Freight Index reported substantial drops on key Transpacific routes, reflecting ongoing downward pressure on ocean freight pricing and market softening worldwide.

headline: Freightos Narrows Q3 Losses on Cost Controls and Revenue Growth
summary: Digital freight booking platform Freightos posted seven point eight million dollars in revenue for the third quarter of twenty twenty-six, marking a two percent year-on-year increase. Through strategic cost-saving measures, the company significantly reduced its financial losses. The IFRS net loss dropped to two point three million dollars compared to five million dollars during the same timeframe last year. Additionally, the adjusted EBITDA loss contracted by fifty-two percent down to one point three million dollars, reflecting improved operational efficiency across its digital logistics network.

headline: Alternative transit corridors boost flexibility over resilience
summary: Ongoing disruptions in major maritime chokepoints like the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz throughout 2026 have forced logistics stakeholders to adopt alternative trade routes. Shippers and governments are increasingly utilizing the Middle Corridor across the Caspian region, the Tehuantepec land bridge in Mexico, and the Northern Sea Route through Russia. While these routes provide greater operational flexibility during crises, experts note they fail to deliver true structural resilience against broader global supply chain vulnerabilities.

headline: Dualog launches maritime AI service to secure seafarer data
summary: Norwegian technology provider Dualog has introduced a specialized artificial intelligence platform tailored for the maritime sector. The new tool aims to provide both onboard crews and shore-based personnel with immediate access to operational insights while maintaining corporate data security. The release responds to recent industry survey data indicating widespread adoption of generic artificial intelligence applications among seafarers for navigation and daily operational tasks, highlighting potential security vulnerabilities in existing maritime communication practices.

headline: HMM Partners with Nextpower on Green Shipping Emissions
summary: South Korean ocean carrier HMM has partnered with American solar technology firm Nextpower through a green shipping initiative. The agreement enables Nextpower to account for carbon emission reductions achieved by HMM's utilization of lower-carbon marine fuels within its broader supply chain reporting framework. This program allows cargo transport customers to claim environmental benefits derived from cleaner alternative marine propulsion options, supporting corporate sustainability targets and regulatory reporting requirements for international maritime freight operations.

headline: Russia-bound cargo ship towed after drone attack
summary: A cargo vessel traveling toward Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad was struck by a drone in the eastern Gulf of Finland, resulting in a fire onboard. The damaged ship drifted into Finnish waters before being towed away by authorities. This maritime security incident highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in regional trade routes and shipping operations within the Baltic Sea corridor, posing potential disruptions to vessel transit and logistics flows in the area.

headline: Tianjin Southwest Maritime Receives Ammonia-Capable Gas Carrier
summary: Tianjin Southwest Maritime has accepted delivery of the André M, a 25,000-cbm gas carrier constructed by CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. The vessel features dual-fuel capability, allowing it to operate on either conventional fuel oil or ammonia, and includes a pre-fitted ammonia bunkering connection. This delivery marks a significant milestone for alternative marine propulsion and sustainable maritime logistics, highlighting ongoing advancements in vessel design to support lower-emission international shipping operations.

headline: Digital workboat chartering platform expands global reach
summary: Digital matching platforms are gaining adoption within the international workboat chartering sector. Following its launch, Nauticworx reports steady growth in completed vessel charters, driven primarily by activity in the North Sea and West Africa. The online system facilitates connections between vessel owners, brokers, and charterers to streamline maritime logistics operations.

headline: China Imported Iron Ore Margins Rebound as Prices Stabilize
summary: Imported iron ore profit margins in China experienced a recovery, shifting back into positive territory. This improvement was supported by a modest increase in port spot prices alongside reduced premiums on specific seaborne shipments. Meanwhile, demand indicators showed a slight contraction, with average daily outbound volumes declining across monitored ports. Market observers anticipate that iron ore prices will remain relatively stable within a defined range in the near term as supply and demand dynamics continue to balance out.

headline: AI Enhances Rather Than Replaces Trucking Dispatchers
summary: Artificial intelligence serves as a powerful force multiplier within the trucking sector by automating routine administrative tasks while preserving essential human oversight in dispatch operations. Industry experts emphasize that technology should be deployed to augment human workers rather than eliminate them, streamlining daily workflows and improving overall efficiency in logistics management.

headline: Asia-US East Coast Ocean Freight Rates Exceed $10,000
summary: Trans-Pacific container shipping rates experienced a slight decline in mid-November, yet they remained drastically elevated compared to the previous year. According to market data from Xeneta, freight rates for routes connecting Asia to the United States East Coast stayed above the ten-thousand-dollar threshold, representing a massive three-hundred percent increase year-over-year. This extreme pricing environment continues to put pressure on maritime logistics and international supply chain budgets for businesses moving goods across the Pacific.

headline: Precious Shipping secures ultramax vessel charter with PACC Line
summary: Thailand-based Precious Shipping has agreed to a year-long charter with Singapore's PACC Line for the 2015-built ultramax vessel Sarita Naree. The agreement spans 11 to 13 months, utilizing an index-linked variable rate that currently equates to approximately $23,700 per day. The 62,964 dwt vessel officially commenced operations under the new charter agreement in late November, reflecting ongoing activity and rate structures within the dry bulk maritime freight sector.

headline: Jinhui Shipping secures higher price for Supramax vessel sale
summary: Hong Kong-based dry bulk shipping firm Jinhui Shipping and Transportation has successfully agreed to sell its 2012-built Supramax vessel, Jin Bi, to Singapore-based Global Pacific Shipping for $17.8 million. This transaction marks a significant increase from an earlier failed attempt to sell the same 56,361 deadweight tonnage bulk carrier for $14.4 million earlier in the year. The Oslo-listed company finalized the deal after signing a formal memorandum of agreement with the new buyer, reflecting shifting market valuations in the dry bulk sector.

headline: Arabian Drilling secures $400m offshore service contract
summary: Arabian Drilling has been awarded a long-term contract valued at approximately $400 million by Khafji Joint Operations. The agreement requires the contractor to supply and operate two self-propelled offshore service units. This deal succeeds previous contracts for two units currently operating in the region. The operational timeline includes a ten-year duration for the first unit, with activities scheduled to begin soon, ensuring continued offshore support and resource extraction operations in the Middle East.

headline: Shipping Corp of India Launches $3.2B Fleet Expansion
summary: State-owned Shipping Corporation of India has initiated a massive $3.2 billion fleet expansion initiative. The Mumbai-listed carrier has issued tenders for up to 22 new vessels, which span gas carriers, tankers, and container ships. Additionally, the company is pursuing secondhand tonnage to bolster its operational capacity across multiple maritime segments.

headline: Aegean Shipping Expands Fleet with COSCO Tanker Order
summary: Aegean Shipping Management has reportedly contracted two additional LR2 product tankers at a shipyard in China, extending its ongoing fleet modernization and expansion initiative through 2030. Industry sources indicate the vessels will feature ice class 1C specifications and are slated for delivery in early 2030. This latest commitment reinforces the company's long-term capital investment strategy within the maritime shipping sector, further strengthening its transport capabilities for future energy and liquid bulk logistics operations.

headline: Maritime conflict expands beyond Black Sea into global trade lanes
summary: The ongoing maritime conflict between Russia and Ukraine has widened significantly, threatening international shipping routes far outside the Black Sea region. Recent incidents include a Russian naval vessel struck in the Libyan port of Benghazi and a sanctioned cargo ship attacked in the Baltic Sea. This geographic expansion raises concerns regarding vessel safety, insurance premiums, and the potential disruption of global maritime logistics as geopolitical tensions increasingly impact international commercial waterways.

headline: Partnership forms to develop nuclear-powered LNG carrier
summary: A consortium including Samsung Heavy Industries, Tesser Atomics, NTNU, and DNV has entered into an agreement to design a nuclear-powered liquefied natural gas carrier concept. The collaborative initiative aims to engineer a demonstration vessel specifically planned for transit routes connecting terminals located in the United States and Europe. This venture seeks to advance alternative propulsion technologies for maritime freight operations, addressing long-term decarbonization and efficiency goals within the global energy shipping sector.

headline: Lufthansa Cargo agrees to buy Fiege Air Cargo Logistics
summary: Lufthansa Cargo has reached an agreement to purchase Fiege Air Cargo Logistics, taking direct control of cargo handling operations at its primary Frankfurt hub. The transaction, signed with current owner Fiege Logistik Stiftung & Co. KG, aims to streamline and manage logistics activities internally. The proposed deal is currently pending regulatory and antitrust clearances before finalization.

headline: Maersk lowers Peak Season Surcharge on India-North America routes
summary: Ocean carrier Maersk has announced a reduction in its Peak Season Surcharge applicable to dry container shipments moving from the Indian Subcontinent to the East and Gulf coasts of the United States and Canada. The adjusted fees will take effect for non-SPOT bookings starting late November 2026. The rate modification impacts key origins including major Indian ports as well as shipments originating from Nepal and Bhutan, excluding specific routings to Houston, providing potential cost relief for shippers utilizing these trade lanes during the period.

headline: Equinor and NCL Extend Low-Carbon Marine Fuel Partnership
summary: Equinor and North Sea Container Line have prolonged their maritime fuel partnership through 2027. Under this continuation, Equinor will supply sustainable bunker fuel from its industrial facility in Norway to power NCL's dual-fuel methanol container ships. This ongoing cooperation supports the transition toward lower-emissions shipping operations within regional maritime logistics.

headline: Samudera and CONCOR Partner to Streamline EXIM Logistics
summary: Container Corporation of India and Samudera have established an agency agreement to enhance coordination between international maritime shipping and inland logistics networks. Formalized in New Delhi, the collaboration focuses on optimizing export and import cargo movements across several key markets, including India, Thailand, and Malaysia. This partnership seeks to improve operational efficiency and connectivity for supply chain stakeholders managing cross-border trade in the region.

headline: FedEx Consortium Completes InPost Acquisition
summary: A consortium led by FedEx, Advent International, A&R Investments, and PPF Group has finalized its buyout of European parcel delivery provider InPost. Following the transaction, the enterprise transitioned to private ownership and was delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Under the updated ownership terms, FedEx and Advent International each maintain a 37 percent stake in the business, strengthening their footprint in the European logistics and parcel delivery sector.

headline: Bureau Veritas Acquires Topo Solutions for AI Supply Chain Tech
summary: Testing and certification provider Bureau Veritas has purchased Hong Kong-based Topo Solutions to enhance its digital offerings for retailers and consumer goods brands. The integration of the artificial intelligence platform aims to improve end-to-end supply chain visibility for clients. Capabilities will span across multiple operational stages, covering raw material sourcing, manufacturing production, regulatory compliance, and quality assurance processes.

headline: Shandong Marine Energy Expands Advanced LNG Fleet
summary: Shandong Marine Energy is broadening its liquefied natural gas carrier fleet by integrating advanced vessel technologies focused on enhancing operational efficiency and maritime safety. The company is collaborating closely with major shipyards, specialized technology providers, and classification partner DNV. Having established its presence in the liquefied gas shipping industry over the past decade, this fleet expansion marks the next phase of its strategic growth in maritime logistics and international energy transport.

headline: Baltic Dry Index Rebounds on Stronger Capesize Rates
summary: The primary maritime freight rate indicator halted a recent two-day decline, increasing by 3.5 percent to reach its highest level since mid-November. This upward movement was largely driven by the capesize segment, which experienced a 6.2 percent jump. The sector, responsible for hauling substantial loads of essential dry commodities such as coal and iron ore, pushed the overall index to 3,000 points, signaling stronger demand in global maritime transportation.

headline: Battery Vessels Proposed to Cut Global Shipping Emissions
summary: Battery-electric vessels have traditionally been restricted to short-distance routes because frequent battery cycling is required for economic viability. A new approach introduces dedicated battery vessels that decouple the energy storage unit from the ship. These systems couple near ports and return to charge, which could potentially address emissions across a much wider segment of the global maritime fleet, overcoming the geographical limits previously facing deep-sea shipping electrification.

headline: IMO Struggles for Compromise on Shipping Emissions Rules
summary: The International Maritime Organization prepares for challenging negotiations concerning its Net-Zero Framework, focusing on a disputed carbon pricing mechanism. These upcoming talks will shape the adoption pace of low-carbon fuels within the maritime sector. Despite mounting consensus regarding the technical standards for marine greenhouse gas reduction, opposition from the United States complicates the path toward a unified global policy for sustainable maritime transport and logistics decarbonization.

headline: Rotterdam alternative bunker fuels lose price advantage
summary: Alternative marine fuels including B100 and liquefied biomethane have experienced a decline in their cost competitiveness compared to conventional very low sulfur fuel oil for intra-European voyages originating from Rotterdam. Decreased FuelEU pooling values contributed to the upward price pressure on these alternative options, as OceanScore's relevant pooling index dropped over the course of the week. This shift reduces the financial incentives previously offered by alternative fuels for maritime operators navigating regional compliance schemes.

headline: IMO renews push for green shipping amid regulatory hurdles
summary: The International Maritime Organization is reviving efforts to achieve net-zero emissions in the maritime transport sector following a previous setback involving the U.S. administration. The renewed push encompasses various alternative technologies and fuels, including wind power, battery systems, e-methanol, and liquefied natural gas. As global logistics networks face mounting pressure to reduce their carbon footprint, international regulators continue to debate viable pathways to decarbonize hard-to-abate maritime freight operations and transition toward sustainable shipping standards.

headline: Belgian Air Traffic Strike Disrupts Peak Cargo Operations
summary: A strike by Belgian air traffic controllers has severely disrupted air freight operations at major hubs in Liège and Brussels just days before the crucial Black Friday shopping period. Approximately 70 cargo flights were impacted as carriers scrambled to reschedule, delay, or divert aircraft to neighboring countries. Airport authorities have not yet confirmed the total number of cancellations or provided a timeline for clearing the backlog of affected freight, posing potential risks to time-sensitive retail supply chains.

headline: Bangladesh garment makers use airfreight after labor unrest
summary: Apparel manufacturers in Bangladesh are utilizing expensive airfreight services to salvage delivery schedules following prolonged labor disruptions that halted production across multiple facilities. The unrest led international buyers to relocate significant confirmed orders to alternative sourcing nations. Industry representatives report substantial financial damages from lost output and canceled contracts, highlighting the vulnerability of the region's textile supply chain to localized labor instability.

headline: IMO's MEPC 85 risks higher shipping costs and regulatory red tape
summary: The maritime sector confronts escalating freight costs, increased regulatory hurdles, and widespread uncertainty if governments fail to establish meaningful economic frameworks during the upcoming International Maritime Organization meeting in London. Experts warn that an over-reliance on technical standards rather than comprehensive economic measures could disrupt critical investments in green fuels and sustainable vessel technology. The outcome of these high-stakes negotiations will significantly impact global maritime decarbonization pathways and long-term operational expenses for ocean carriers.

headline: EU Caps on Chinese Hybrids Threaten Vehicle Logistics
summary: Proposed European Union restrictions on imported Chinese hybrid vehicles pose significant challenges for finished vehicle logistics providers operating in the region. This market segment has recently driven substantial activity for automotive transport networks. Despite the impending disruptions aimed at safeguarding domestic vehicle manufacturers, industry associations express confidence in the sector's operational adaptability to navigate regulatory shifts and changing trade flows across the European automotive supply chain.

headline: US Final-Mile Delivery Costs Surge Past Inflation Rates
summary: Recent data from a logistics index reveals that final-mile delivery expenses in the United States increased by over ten percent year-on-year during the second and third quarters, outpacing general consumer price inflation significantly. Logistics providers and carriers report that these escalating operational expenses are growing at a much faster rate than their revenues, creating ongoing financial pressures across the sector as costs continue an upward trajectory observed since 2019.

headline: Retailers shift from peak season to year-round optimization
summary: Retail businesses are transforming their operational approaches by moving away from traditional peak season preparations in favor of continuous, year-round supply chain optimization. Organizations possessing robust and adaptable fulfillment networks are better positioned to handle unexpected disruptions and successfully navigate high-demand periods. This strategic shift emphasizes the importance of building resilience and flexibility into inventory and distribution operations to maintain a competitive advantage throughout the entire annual cycle.

headline: AI Adoption in Air Cargo Drives Margin Optimization
summary: Following successful data digitization efforts, the air cargo sector is increasingly adopting artificial intelligence to enhance operational decision-making. Industry stakeholders are leveraging these advanced technologies to reduce operating costs, increase revenue potential, and mitigate risks that impact profit margins across freight networks.

headline: Lufthansa Cargo acquires second ground handler at Frankfurt
summary: Lufthansa Cargo is actively securing dedicated handling capacity at Frankfurt airport by acquiring a second ground agent. This strategic move allows the carrier to exercise greater control over its warehouse and distribution operations at one of its primary global hubs, ensuring streamlined cargo flow and enhanced service reliability amid fluctuating international freight demands.

headline: US rule on ship-to-ship transfers tightens Gulf oil blockade
summary: A recent United States regulatory measure regarding ship-to-ship oil transfers has intensified the ongoing constraints surrounding the Strait of Hormuz. While maintaining pressure on regional trade routes, this policy effectively transfers operational and financial risks directly onto the commercial vessels responsible for transporting petroleum out of the Persian Gulf. This development highlights the growing intersection of maritime logistics, geopolitical tensions, and regulatory enforcement affecting global energy supply chains.

headline: MSC Adds Busan Stop to Pearl Transpacific Route
summary: Mediterranean Shipping Company has integrated Busan into the westbound leg of its weekly Pearl container service connecting the Far East with the United States West Coast. The South Korean port will be incorporated into the rotation following calls at Los Angeles and Oakland, prior to vessels proceeding onward to Hai Phong, Vietnam. The maritime shipping loop utilizes a fleet of seven container vessels with capacities varying between 7,800 and larger container units, enhancing connectivity across these key international trade gateways.

headline: Ocean Network Express to Launch KCJ Container Service
summary: Ocean Network Express is set to introduce a weekly maritime route connecting South Korea, China, and Jakarta starting in late November. Designated as the KCJ service, this deployment will utilize six container vessels with capacities around 4,500 TEU each. The new maritime offering will succeed the company's existing slot arrangement on an alternative joint service, streamlining operations and expanding proprietary vessel deployment across these key Asian trade corridors.

headline: Maersk announces blank sailing on Asia-Latin America route
summary: Container shipping line Maersk has scheduled a blank sailing on its ASAS service, which links Far East Asia with the East Coast of South America. The carrier stated that the capacity reduction is a response to cargo seasonality and shifting demand patterns. The disruption impacts westbound voyage 652W, originating in Shanghai in December 2026, alongside the corresponding eastbound voyage, as part of ongoing network adjustments to manage fluctuating trade volumes.

headline: Semaf cancels Renfe driver strike following Spanish ministry agreement
summary: The Spanish train drivers union Semaf has officially canceled the upcoming strike originally scheduled for late November. The industrial action would have caused significant disruptions across the national rail network, directly impacting the operations of Renfe Mercancias freight transport services. The cancellation comes after a successful agreement was reached with the Spanish ministry, averting potential supply chain bottlenecks and cargo delivery delays throughout the country's rail freight sector.

headline: Hapag-Lloyd Imposes Vietnam Equipment Surcharge
summary: Ocean carrier Hapag-Lloyd has announced a new Equipment Imbalance Surcharge targeting intra-Asia shipments destined for Vietnam. The additional fee applies to both dry and refrigerated containers across various sizes, including twenty-foot and forty-foot units. The pricing adjustment takes effect for sailings starting on December 1, 2026, and will remain active until further notice. Surcharges are set at fifty dollars for standard twenty-foot dry boxes and one hundred dollars for forty-foot dry and high-cube containers, reflecting ongoing container repositioning costs and equipment flow imbalances within the regional shipping network.

headline: Maersk raises intermodal fuel fees for UK and Ireland
summary: Maersk has updated its intermodal fuel fee structures for full-container-load landside transportation across the United Kingdom and Ireland for December 2026. The adjusted fees apply to domestic logistics operations. In the United Kingdom, the surcharge for cargo moved by either truck or rail is set at 11.6 percent. Meanwhile, logistics transport conducted via truck within Ireland will incur a fuel fee of 8.1 percent. These adjustments impact shippers utilizing combined transport modes within the two regions.

headline: Weakening Refining Margins Pressure Global Tanker Freight Rates
summary: Cracks are beginning to emerge in the tanker freight market as declining refining margins make elevated shipping costs increasingly difficult to absorb. According to recent industry reports, refining margins have dropped significantly this month, with Asian gasoline margins hovering near three-year lows and approaching negative territory. This compression in profitability is squeezing the room available for charterers to pay current freight rates, signaling potential shifts in maritime transport demand and pricing dynamics across the energy supply chain.

headline: Asia-US container rates drop amid LA/LB strike threat
summary: Ocean shipping rates for containers traveling from East Asia and China to the United States have generally declined. The downturn occurs as the maritime logistics industry closely monitors the potential for a labor strike this weekend at the critical ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. Meanwhile, liquid chemical tanker rates originating from the US Gulf experienced an upward trend. Industry stakeholders remain alert as negotiations and the looming disruption threaten West Coast port operations and cargo flow.

headline: Capesize Dry Bulk Market Experiences Mixed, Softer Week
summary: The dry bulk shipping market faced a downward trend for Capesize vessels over the week, driven by initial weakness in the Pacific region. Despite a temporary midweek recovery that helped stabilize sentiment, the Baltic Capesize Index fluctuated and ultimately closed lower than its Monday opening level. Market conditions remained generally softer as fluctuating rates weighed on overall performance.

headline: IEA Highlights Extreme Weather Vulnerabilities in Energy Shipping
summary: The International Energy Agency reports that global energy transport relies heavily on maritime routes, with a significant portion of crude oil, petroleum products, and natural gas moving by water. However, these vital maritime supply chains face growing disruptions from extreme weather events and natural hazards. Such environmental factors threaten the steady flow of international energy commodities from producers to consumers, highlighting vulnerabilities in the global energy distribution network.

headline: Middle East Clean Tanker Rates Show Mixed Regional Trends
summary: Eastbound freight rates for clean LR2 tankers experienced significant growth last week, driven by a sharp climb in Middle East Gulf to Japan routes. This surge lifted overall Baltic round-trip time charter equivalents notably. In contrast, westbound and Mediterranean routes demonstrated softer performance, with voyages to the UK-Continent seeing a decline. These diverging regional movements highlight shifting demand patterns within maritime liquid bulk logistics and freight markets.

headline: Sanctioned tankers deliver millions of barrels to Yemen terminal
summary: Between September and November 2026, maritime intelligence identified twelve sanctioned oil tankers delivering approximately 3.26 million barrels of fuel to the Houthi-controlled Ras Issa terminal on the Red Sea coast of Yemen. The vast majority of these vessels attempted to evade detection by operating with their automatic identification systems switched off or by broadcasting false geographic positions, highlighting ongoing illicit maritime trade activities and evasion tactics within critical regional energy supply routes.

headline: Diamond Line Doubles Piraeus-Constanta Shipping Frequency
summary: Diamond Line, an intra-European subsidiary of COSCO Shipping Lines, has increased the frequency of its Piraeus-Constanta Express maritime service from once to twice a week. The carrier introduced a second vessel to the route to enhance sailing availability between Greece and Romania. The established port rotation connecting Piraeus and Constanta remains unaffected by the capacity and schedule expansion, improving regional supply chain connectivity and transit options for freight moving through these key maritime hubs.

headline: Pan Continental and PanStar launch PHX container service
summary: Pan Continental and PanStar are introducing a weekly container service linking South Korea, Vietnam, and China. Named the PHX service, the operation will utilize two container ships with capacities ranging from 700 to 1,000 TEU. Additionally, CK Line has secured slot charters on this new maritime route. The deployment aims to enhance intra-Asian container shipping connectivity and capacity across key trade hubs in the region.

headline: Claus-Peter Offen orders four 7,000 TEU container ships from GSI
summary: German shipowner Claus-Peter Offen has contracted Guangzhou Shipyard International in China to build four 7,000 TEU container vessels, with delivery slated for 2030. The conventionally powered ships are backed by seven-year charter agreements secured with German carrier Hapag-Lloyd. This fleet expansion highlights ongoing investments in maritime transport capacity and long-term vessel chartering within the global container shipping sector.

headline: Cool Carriers adds world-first gate-rudder reefer vessel
summary: Cool Carriers has expanded its fleet with the delivery of the Snow Land, an ice-class refrigerated cargo ship built by Kitanihon Shipbuilding in Japan. This vessel represents the third addition to a planned seven-ship Snow-class program. Notably, the Snow Land is equipped with an innovative gate rudder system, marking the first time a specialized reefer vessel utilizes this advanced technology as an alternative to conventional rudder designs, enhancing the efficiency and maneuverability of maritime logistics operations.

headline: Swire Shipping lowers feeder surcharges for Indian Subcontinent
summary: Swire Shipping has announced a reduction in its Feeder and Equipment Surcharge specifically targeting selected trades across the Indian Subcontinent. The updated fee structure will take effect for all Bills of Lading carrying an on-board date starting November 20, 2026. Meanwhile, services governed by the United States Federal Maritime Commission will continue to follow standard regulatory notification timelines before any adjustments are implemented. This move impacts regional maritime freight costs and shipping logistics for businesses operating within these trade lanes.

headline: San Pedro Bay Ports Advance Zero-Emission Clean Air Plan
summary: The ports of Long Beach and Los Angeles are launching the next phase of their long-standing Clean Air Action Plan, marking two decades of environmental initiatives. This updated strategy focuses on accelerating the transition toward completely zero-emission port operations. Over the past twenty years, the ports have achieved significant reductions in air pollution through collaborative regional sustainability programs, and these new efforts aim to further green supply chain and maritime logistics activities in Southern California.

headline: Mexican Truckers Secure Highway Safety Agreements
summary: Mexican freight transportation associations have successfully negotiated twenty-nine new agreements with government officials designed to enhance security along major highways. These commitments follow a nationwide strike organized by commercial drivers to protest escalating safety concerns and demanding better operating conditions for the logistics sector across the country.

headline: Valenciaport Reports Steady Container Traffic and Growth in Rail
summary: Container volumes at the Port Authority of València remained stable over the past twelve months, registering a modest 0.15 percent increase to total over 5.6 million TEUs. Meanwhile, intermodal operations experienced substantial growth, with rail-handled TEUs jumping more than 20 percent compared to the previous year. Additionally, vehicle shipments processed as cargo through the port facilities increased by nine percent, highlighting positive momentum across specific segments of the maritime logistics hub.

headline: Sidra Line Realigns Mediterranean–West Africa Route
summary: Sidra Line has announced updates to its Mediterranean–West Africa maritime route, adjusting port calls to optimize regional connectivity. The carrier is expanding its service by adding stops in Misurata, Libya, Rades, Tunisia, and Casablanca, Morocco. Concurrently, the rotation will drop Adana, while maintaining connections to Conakry in Guinea utilizing a 750 TEU vessel.

headline: JSV Logistic Restores Direct Turkey-Canary Islands Service
summary: Logistics provider JSV Logistic has brought back the direct Canary Islands route within its weekly Turkey to Spain shipping operation. The archipelago leg had been temporarily detached from the network. To support the reinstated route, the company expanded capacity by deploying three container vessels with capacities ranging from 750 to 1,200 TEU, enhancing maritime connectivity between Turkish ports and the Spanish islands.

headline: Backup carriers raise rates as market tightens for shippers
summary: Shippers utilizing contingency carriers as part of their backup strategies are facing rising costs. As market conditions tighten, secondary transportation providers are no longer readily available on standby without increased pricing. Organizations relying on alternative logistics networks must navigate higher expenditures to secure capacity when primary carriers face disruptions, impacting overall freight and distribution budgets.

headline: Port of LA issues environmental report for terminal upgrade
summary: The Port of Los Angeles has published a draft environmental impact assessment concerning proposed upgrades at the Wilmington marine oil terminal managed by Phillips 66. The document serves to gather stakeholder feedback prior to the development of a final environmental report. This infrastructure initiative involves specific modifications at Berths 148 to 151 aimed at improving facility operations and environmental compliance within the key maritime shipping hub.

headline: MSC Updates Ecuador-NWC-USA Service Port Rotation
summary: MSC has announced updates to its Ecuador-Northwest Continent-USA shipping service, reinstating calls at St. Petersburg, Rotterdam, and Jacksonville. These three ports were previously cut from the route in July of the current year. Under the revised schedule, Jacksonville will be integrated into the westbound transatlantic portion of the voyage, while Klaipeda has been removed entirely from the port rotation. This adjustment alters the connectivity between South American production points, European hubs, and United States ports.

headline: Lloyd's Register Clears Nuclear Ship Rules
summary: New classification standards have been established to govern the integration of nuclear power systems into commercial vessels and offshore assets. Developed by Lloyd's Register, this framework provides essential evaluation guidelines for adopting nuclear energy across various ship types, representing a notable development for maritime logistics and propulsion technology in the shipping sector.

headline: Maersk Postpones Australia-New Zealand Shipping Policy
summary: Ocean carrier Maersk has pushed back the full enforcement date of its No Shipping Instruction, No Load Policy for export cargo originating in Australia and New Zealand. The strict enforcement was initially scheduled to begin following an introductory soft launch phase. However, the carrier decided to extend the transition period and has not yet established a new firm deadline for implementing the policy. This regulatory adjustment affects regional freight forwarders and shippers managing containerized exports across the Australasian market.

headline: MSC Launches Two New Regional Services in Asia and Middle East
summary: Mediterranean Shipping Company is enhancing its regional maritime network by introducing two distinct shipping routes targeting the Arabian Gulf and the Indian Subcontinent. Slated for a December launch, the Fujairah Shuttle 2 will establish connections between Colombo, Khor Fakkan, and Fujairah. Additionally, the carrier is rolling out a direct maritime service linking Ennore in India directly with Chittagong in Bangladesh, aimed at improving transit efficiency and regional trade flows across these key South Asian and Middle Eastern corridors.

headline: Caerus Shipping Introduces Direct Oman-India Maritime Service
summary: Caerus Shipping has launched the Arab Sea Express, a bi-weekly maritime service connecting the port of Sohar in Oman with the Indian ports of Nhava Sheva and Mundra. This new direct route aims to improve ocean freight options and connectivity for exporters, importers, freight forwarders, and non-vessel-operating common carriers moving cargo between the two countries, streamlining regional supply chain operations.

headline: Maersk implements 15 percent fuel surcharge for Cyprus trucking
summary: Maersk announced a temporary 15 percent fuel surcharge on all truck transportation services within Cyprus, effective late November 2026. The carrier stated that the adjustment is a direct response to escalating fuel expenses driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The fee will be designated on customer billing invoices as either an Export Fuel Surcharge or an Import Fuel Surcharge based on shipment direction.

headline: Tentative union agreement avoids strike at major US container port
summary: A provisional labor accord has successfully prevented a potential work stoppage at the nation's largest container port hub. This breakthrough follows more than twelve months of intense contract discussions and federally facilitated mediation, ultimately removing a significant disruption threat to domestic import and export operations on the West Coast.

headline: DHL Express launches AI-powered customs clearance tool
summary: DHL Express has rolled out a new artificial intelligence tool designed to help small international shippers determine accurate product identifiers for cross-border customs clearance. The technology aims to remove guesswork and streamline the compliance process for smaller businesses engaged in international trade, reducing potential delays and administrative burdens at international borders by automating product classification.

headline: Akkon Lines introduces Türkiye-Levant container route
summary: Akkon Lines is set to roll out a new maritime container route linking Türkiye with Syria and Lebanon starting in December 2026. Designated as the Levant Bridge Service, the operation will utilize one small vessel to maintain a ten-day sailing frequency. The route establishes direct connections among three Turkish ports, Latakia, and Beirut, enhancing regional maritime logistics and shipping connectivity across the Eastern Mediterranean basin.

headline: Seatrium secures S$12.2B order book amid new contract wins
summary: Singapore-based marine engineering and offshore energy firm Seatrium has announced a net order book totaling S$12.2 billion as of September 2026, driven by recent contract acquisitions. The company accumulated S$1.7 billion in new orders over the course of the year. The current order portfolio includes 35 active projects, with fulfillment and deliveries slated through 2033.

headline: CMA CGM Expands India West Coast Coverage on PIKEX2 Route
summary: Maritime carrier CMA CGM has integrated the port of Hazira into its weekly Pakistan Khalifa Express 2 container shipping route. This network adjustment broadens regional trade connectivity along the western coast of India. The service utilizes two container vessels with capacities ranging from 1,700 to 2,500 TEU, linking key maritime hubs in India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka to support regional logistics and freight movement.

headline: Eimskip Orders Konecranes Mobile Harbor Crane for Iceland
summary: Icelandic shipping and logistics provider Eimskip has placed an order for a new Konecranes Gottwald ESP.8 Mobile Harbor Crane destined for the port of Reyðarfjörður. Booked during the final quarter of the year, the equipment delivery is planned for the third quarter of the following year. The infrastructure addition is designed to enhance cargo handling capabilities at the facility, supporting the processing of containerized shipments as well as general and project cargo operations.

headline: Zim Reports Q3 Profit Surge Driven by Higher Freight Rates
summary: Container shipping company Zim recorded a significant third-quarter net profit of $830 million, bolstered by a 55 percent increase in freight rates. Following this strong financial performance, the carrier upgraded its annual earnings outlook and announced a substantial dividend payout for shareholders. Meanwhile, the company continues to await regulatory approvals regarding its planned acquisition by Hapag-Lloyd, which would reshape its future market positioning and operational footprint within the global maritime shipping sector.

headline: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern merger faces scrutiny
summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern are actively defending their proposed coast-to-coast railroad merger amidst ongoing regulatory review. The consolidation effort has received backing from labor unions, yet it continues to draw significant apprehension from shippers regarding potential impacts on service quality, competition, and operational efficiency across the rail network. Federal regulators are currently weighing these competing interests as the review process moves forward.

headline: West London Orbital proposal threatens freight rail capacity
summary: The Rail Freight Group has raised concerns that the planned West London Orbital passenger railway could compromise vital freight access and transport capacity in the region. Industry representatives are urging planners to ensure that future passenger infrastructure developments do not negatively impact the flow of goods or diminish the availability of essential freight train paths across the network.

headline: PKP Cargo Faces Operational Capacity Risks Amid Coal Mandates
summary: Polish authorities cleared former executives of criminal wrongdoing regarding a 2022 mandate requiring the freight operator to prioritize coal transport. The policy decision has left the company facing severe risks to its ongoing operating capacity. The situation highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in European rail logistics when state-directed energy mandates conflict with commercial freight strategy and operational viability.

headline: Rail freight removes HS2 Euston excavation material
summary: Rail freight transport is actively utilized to clear up to 170,000 tonnes of excavated material from the high-speed rail construction site located at Euston. This logistics approach effectively eliminates a significant volume of heavy road transport movements from the area, mitigating urban congestion and reducing carbon emissions associated with construction waste removal for the major infrastructure project.

headline: Italian rail freight disrupted by 23-hour national strike
summary: Rail freight operations across Italy are scheduled to halt entirely for 23 hours due to a nationwide labor strike. The stoppage will begin in the evening and last nearly a full day, causing significant disruptions to domestic and cross-border rail logistics networks, freight transit schedules, and supply chain movements throughout the country until normal operations resume the following evening.

headline: Mexico Introduces Digital Trucking Compliance Rules
summary: Mexico has launched new regulatory requirements for trucking operators pursuing voluntary certification. The initiative is designed to enhance highway safety standards and ensure stricter operational compliance across the domestic freight sector. Transport companies must now adhere to updated digital protocols to achieve and maintain their certified status under the program, reflecting ongoing efforts to modernize logistics oversight and improve transport security throughout the country's extensive highway network.

headline: Delta Cargo Airlifts Drought Relief Supplies to Puerto Rico
summary: Delta Cargo collaborated with New York State officials and charitable organizations to transport nearly 11,000 pounds of essential supplies to San Juan, Puerto Rico. The emergency shipment included critical food, water, and medical resources to assist communities affected by severe drought conditions on the island this year. The logistics effort highlights humanitarian air freight operations in response to regional environmental crises.

headline: Geodis Secures WHO GDP Certification for APAC Healthcare
summary: Logistics provider Geodis has earned World Health Organization Good Distribution Practices certification for its network across the Asia Pacific region. This accreditation validates the company's quality management systems and adherence to international standards designed to preserve the safety, quality, and integrity of pharmaceutical products as they move through the supply chain. The milestone enhances the company's capabilities within the regulated healthcare logistics sector across multiple markets in the region.

headline: Fujairah Fuel Oil Inventories Increase Slightly in November
summary: Inventories of fuel oil at the Middle Eastern storage and bunkering hub of Fujairah have posted a modest one percent increase during the first half of November compared to the previous month's averages. Data from the local oil industry zone and S&P Global indicates that the growth is driven primarily by gains in heavy distillate and residual inventories, which rose by 42,000 barrels to reach 4.49 million barrels, alongside smaller upward movements in middle distillate supplies.

headline: IMO to weigh net-zero framework amid decarbonization debate
summary: The International Maritime Organization is preparing for upcoming negotiations regarding its Net-Zero Framework. Committee members face a critical decision between adopting a softer regulatory approach to resolve ongoing deadlocks or maintaining stringent standards to ensure meaningful emissions reductions. The outcome of the upcoming meetings will significantly influence the maritime industry's long-term sustainability trajectory and operational compliance timelines for global shipping networks.

headline: Indian ship recycling market weakens on currency shifts
summary: The ship recycling market in India experienced a downturn over the week, driven largely by ongoing currency fluctuations. These monetary shifts led to reduced purchasing activity and softer market conditions overall. Such volatility impacts the broader maritime asset liquidation and scrap metal supply chains operating within the region.

headline: Panda Express Line Restructures Russian Far East Network
summary: Maritime carrier Panda Express Line has implemented a comprehensive reorganization of four shipping loops connecting the Russian Far East with ports in China and South Korea. The adjustments involve a redistribution of port coverage across the PEL2, PEL4, PEL5, and PEL6 services. Key updates include the replacement of Tianjin with Ningbo and Busan on the PEL2 route, the reinstatement of Tianjin alongside the addition of Dalian on the PEL4 service, and new port introductions on the PEL5 loop to optimize regional connectivity and operational efficiency.

headline: FESCO Drops Da Nang and Yantian from China-Russia Route
summary: Maritime transport operator FESCO has dropped Da Nang and Shenzhen's Yantian terminal from its FCDL1 shipping service. The route links Vietnam and southern China to the Russian Far East port of Vladivostok. Following this network adjustment, the loop maintains calls at Ho Chi Minh City, Hai Phong, and Nansha. This operational change alters the direct maritime connectivity between key manufacturing hubs in Vietnam and China and the Russian market.

headline: Maersk introduces heavy-load surcharge for China to South America route
summary: Ocean carrier Maersk has announced a new heavy-load surcharge of $200 per container for maritime shipments moving from China to South America. The fee takes effect in December 2026 and applies to cargo originating from major Chinese ports including Shanghai, Qingdao, Xingang, and Dalian when the Verified Gross Mass surpasses 23 metric tonnes. Target destination ports include key hubs in Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina. The measure aims to manage vessel weight distribution and operational costs on this major trade lane.

headline: DP World Ups Investment in Mozambique's Port of Maputo
summary: DP World has increased its financial commitment to the Port of Maputo to 200 million United States dollars, raising its previous pledge of 165 million. This expanded funding follows discussions between the company's executive leadership and the President of Mozambique. The capital injection aims to enhance the port's infrastructure, boosting regional trade capabilities and strengthening the country's strategic trade position within Southern Africa.

headline: MSC Expands Mediterranean-Canada Service to Greece and Türkiye
summary: MSC has broadened its weekly Med Canadian Service to directly link the Eastern Mediterranean with Montreal. The updated shipping route features port calls in Türkiye at Tekirdag, Gemlik, and Aliaga, alongside Piraeus in Greece, prior to transiting the Western Mediterranean toward Canada. To support this network expansion, the carrier has deployed a fleet of seven container vessels to maintain regular operational frequency on the corridor.

headline: KMTC and Namsung halt joint South Korea-Japan container route
summary: Container carriers KMTC and Namsung Shipping have halted their jointly operated weekly JPS1/BJS service linking ports in South Korea and Japan. The route previously utilized two container ships with a capacity of roughly 1,000 TEU, equally provided by both shipping companies. The affected port rotation included stops in Busan, Hakata, Kanazawa, Kushiro, Tomakomai, Sapporo, and Akita before returning to Busan. This suspension reduces direct maritime logistics capacity between the two neighboring countries.

headline: Arabian Gulf Crude Oil Exports Drop Significantly Amid Conflict
summary: Crude oil exports from the Arabian Gulf experienced a substantial decline over a ten-month period, dropping by over twenty-seven percent. According to industry reports, regional loading volumes were severely impacted by ongoing geopolitical conflict in Iran. This sharp reduction contrasts with broader global crude loading trends, which saw a modest year-over-year increase during the same timeframe, highlighting the localized disruption to maritime energy logistics and international trade flows originating from the key Middle Eastern export hub.

headline: IMO's MEPC 85 convenes to address shipping decarbonization divide
summary: Delegates from the International Maritime Organization will gather in London for the Marine Environment Protection Committee meeting to negotiate a landmark agreement on maritime decarbonization. The session takes place amid mounting pressure to bridge existing divisions among member states regarding the sector's climate transition strategy and green shipping targets.

headline: Baltic Dry Index Drops Second Consecutive Session on Lower Rates
summary: The primary shipping freight benchmark experienced a second straight daily decline, dipping slightly to 2,898 points. The downturn was driven by decreases across major vessel categories, including the capesize segment, which handles large shipments of essential raw materials like coal and iron ore, as well as the supramax index.

headline: SAL Heavy Lift and DNV expand maritime partnership
summary: SAL Heavy Lift and DNV are deepening their long-standing partnership to enhance heavy-lift shipping operations and vessel development. The collaboration encompasses classification services, newbuilding support, and advisory expertise, notably contributing to the design and rollout of SAL's Orca Class vessels. Additionally, the initiative integrates advanced digital tools like the Route-Specific Cargo Calculator to streamline day-to-day maritime logistics, improve cargo planning efficiency, and maintain high operational standards across a substantial fleet of specialized cargo vessels.

headline: Container Ship Time Charter Index Holds Steady in Week 47
summary: The container shipping charter market experienced overall stability during the forty-seventh week of the year. According to the latest assessment data released by the Hamburg and Bremen shipbrokers association, the market demonstrated only minimal movement and limited week-on-week gains across various vessel segments. This indicates steady demand and ongoing rate equilibrium within global maritime logistics as carriers navigate current trade conditions.

headline: Drewry World Container Index Falls 3 Percent
summary: The benchmark global container index dropped three percent over the past week, according to recent data. The widely followed metric serves as a key reference for procurement professionals managing ocean freight contracts and provides insights into fluctuating market conditions across major international trade lanes. Analysts continuously track these rate movements to help organizations evaluate shipping costs and optimize their global logistics strategies in response to shifting maritime pricing trends.

headline: IMO Talks Resume Amid High EU Shipping Carbon Costs
summary: Delegates gather in London for international maritime greenhouse gas negotiations as a new study estimates the annual European Union emissions trading system bill for shipowners will reach approximately nine billion euros. The research highlights that most member states are not mandated to reinvest these carbon revenues back into the maritime sector, with only two exceptions noted. These financial pressures set the backdrop for ongoing discussions to establish a global carbon pricing mechanism for shipping.

headline: Subsea 7 Seeks Buyer for Vessel Ahead of Saipem Merger
